finding.claim: Stored second-order SSRF: the unvalidated `icon` parameter of PUT /profile is persisted to iconUrl and later fetched server-side with an HTTP GET by the nightly sync() job, allowing requests to arbitrary http/https hosts including internal addresses and cloud metadata endpoints.
finding.source: Profile.update(String webhook, String icon) at src/Profile.java:11 (entry per comment at line 10: PUT /profile); icon stored unvalidated at src/Profile.java:16
finding.sink: HttpClient.send(HttpRequest.newBuilder().uri(URI.create(iconUrl)).GET().build(), ...) at src/Profile.java:23-24, invoked from sync() at src/Profile.java:20

trace.note: Entry comment: PUT /profile handler (route wiring not in repo)
icon stored into this.iconUrl with no validation
nightly sync(HttpClient c) runs later, reads stored iconUrl
URI.create(iconUrl) and GET sent from server network position
response body read to byte array and discarded (blind SSRF)

finding.guards_checked: No validation on icon at write (Profile.java:11-16) or use (Profile.java:23). Java HttpClient rejects non-http(s) schemes, so file: is not reachable; any http/https host/IP is reachable. Webhook regex at Profile.java:12 is SAFE for the webhook sink (anchored, fixed host hooks.example.com, no userinfo/query/port). Uncertain: HttpClient c is constructed outside this repo; if redirects are followed, a hooks.example.com redirect could reach internal hosts (not verified, not reported).

verdict.guard_found: none. The icon parameter is stored unvalidated at src/Profile.java:16 and used directly in URI.create(iconUrl) at src/Profile.java:23 with no scheme, host, or regex check. The only validation, the webhook regex at src/Profile.java:12, applies to webhook, not icon.
verdict.reason: The trace matches the file: update() takes icon from the PUT /profile handler (comment at src/Profile.java:10, parameter at :11), stores it unvalidated at :16, and sync() fetches it with a server-side GET at :23-24, with no closing guard. The one caveat is that the PUT route wiring is outside the repo, so whether an unprivileged user can reach it is inferred from the comment, not verified; I treated it as user-facing because a profile field is the normal low-privilege path.
